Field Value PRI facility and the level of the entry: DEBUG 7, INFO 6, WARNING 4, ERROR 3 TIMESTAMP Time of the entry (UTC) HOSTNAME kiosk.name (characters other than printable ASCII replaced by _) APP-NAME pandora-box MSGID Name of the event (device_verdict, infected_files...)

Over TCP and TLS, the messages are framed by octet counting (RFC 5425, RFC 6587), as syslog over TLS requires.

format = "json": the JSON entry alone, one per line over TCP and TLS, one per datagram over UDP. This suits receivers of JSON lines (Logstash json_lines, Fluent Bit, Vector) and SIEMs that decode the JSON of a raw message.

Every entry holds timestamp, level, kiosk and event, then the fields of the event. The timestamps come from the clock of the kiosk, synchronized by NTP in the profile online (Time).

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
transport Default port tls 6514 Recommended: the certificate of the SIEM is verified (certificate authorities of ca, host name of host), TLS 1.2 at least tcp 514 Clear text, on a trusted network only udp 514 Clear text; a datagram may be lost without notice

The kiosk does not authenticate itself with a client certificate.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
The log file is the queue. The service saves the position of the last entry sent (/var/lib/pandora-box-siem/state.json): when the SIEM cannot be reached, it tries again (after 1 second, then twice longer each time, up to 1 minute) and sends every entry logged meanwhile, in order. The same applies when the service or the kiosk restarts. logrotate moves the log file every month: the service sends the end of the moved file before the new one, so an outage longer than a month loses the entries of the oldest month.

Syslog has no acknowledgment: over TCP and TLS, the entries sent just before a connection breaks may be lost, or sent twice when it is broken while they are sent. Over UDP, nothing is guaranteed.

docs.title: The service
docs.text:
pandora-box-siem.service (src/pandora_box/siem.py) follows the log file and sends its entries. It exits at once when [siem] is disabled.

  • The kiosk itself has no network (IPAddressDeny=any, no IP socket): it only writes the log file. The service runs as the pandora-box-siem user, without privileges and in a systemd sandbox, and the firewall lets that user out (TCP and UDP) besides the update service.
  • It reads the log file through the pandora-box-log group, the group of /var/log/pandora-box and of the files of the kiosk: it can read neither the scan reports nor the quarantine (/var/lib/pandora-box, mode 0700).
  • Its messages, connection lost and back, are in its journal: journalctl -u pandora-box-siem.

docs.title: Receivers
docs.text:
Wazuh: the manager receives syslog over TCP or UDP, without TLS, from the addresses it allows (<remote> of ossec.conf, connection syslog). With format = "json" and transport = "tcp", each entry reaches the JSON decoder of Wazuh as is; check the decoding with wazuh-logtest.

rsyslog, over TLS (packages rsyslog and rsyslog-gnutls):

global(
    DefaultNetstreamDriverCAFile="/etc/rsyslog.d/ca.pem"
    DefaultNetstreamDriverCertFile="/etc/rsyslog.d/siem.pem"
    DefaultNetstreamDriverKeyFile="/etc/rsyslog.d/siem.key"
)
module(load="imtcp" StreamDriver.Name="gtls" StreamDriver.Mode="1"
       StreamDriver.AuthMode="anon")
input(type="imtcp" port="6514")

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
The service runs outside of the image too, with any configuration whose [siem] is enabled, here towards a local receiver:

nc -lk 5514 &
pandora-box-siem --config pandora-box.toml --state /tmp/siem-state.json

with host = "127.0.0.1", transport = "tcp" and port = 5514. The virtual machine test sends the logs of the kiosk to a syslog receiver of the test (Testing with QEMU).

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text: The detection engines of a kiosk only use a signed signature set, verified at each start. A set is installed from a signature update device (a USB key holding a set, for kiosks without network) or, when it is enabled, online. Without a valid set, the kiosk scans nothing: it shows NO VALID SIGNATURES and waits for a signature update device.

docs.title: In short
docs.text:
On the computer that holds the update key, for instance every day:

export ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY=...
publish/publish.sh /srv/pandora-box/pandora-box-signatures /secure/update.key
cp -r /srv/pandora-box/pandora-box-signatures /media/$USER/KEY/

Insert the key into the kiosk: it installs the set, reloads its engines and asks to remove the key. An online kiosk does it by itself every 6 hours.

docs.title: Updating a kiosk
docs.text:
Copy a signed set into a pandora-box-signatures folder at the root of a USB key (vfat, exFAT, NTFS or ext4) and insert it into the kiosk. The kiosk verifies and installs the set, reloads its engines, then asks to remove the key: a signature update device is never scanned, so do not use it to carry other files.

The kiosk shows and logs the result (signatures_installed, signatures_refused with the reason, or signatures_not_newer). A set is only installed when it is newer than the installed one.

The kiosk warns when its signatures get old (see Signature freshness).

docs.title: Preparing a set
docs.text:
pandora-box-signatures publish downloads the signatures of every engine from their sources, checks that the engines of a kiosk can load them, then builds and signs a set (src/pandora_box/publish.py):

Source Files Notes clamav clamav/main.cvd, daily, bytecode updated by freshclam (incremental), which verifies their Cisco Talos signature yara-forge yara/yara-forge/yara-rules-core.yar YARA Forge "core" package, latest GitHub release signature-base yara/signature-base/*.yar opt-in: YARA Forge already includes its rules malwarebazaar malwarebazaar/malwarebazaar.sha256.bin full SHA-256 export, needs a free abuse.ch Auth-Key (ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY) hashlookup hashlookup/hashlookup-full.bloom about 1 GB, published monthly

The publication runs in a container holding freshclam, clamscan and the engines, for instance every day on the computer that holds the signing key:

export ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY=...
publish/publish.sh /srv/pandora-box/pandora-box-signatures /secure/update.key
cp -r /srv/pandora-box/pandora-box-signatures /media/KEY/

Downloads are HTTPS only and cached (--cache, default ~/.cache/pandora-box-signatures): a source that did not change (ETag, Last-Modified) is not downloaded again. Before signing, the set is loaded with the engines of the kiosk: the YARA rules must compile with YARA-X, the MalwareBazaar database and the Hashlookup filter must load, and clamscan must load the ClamAV databases. A set that fails is never signed, and the previous output folder is kept: a broken set, validly signed, would make every kiosk that installs it unable to scan. The set must contain the files of every engine enabled on the kiosks: a kiosk refuses to scan with a set that misses one.

The full set is about 1.2 GB (ClamAV about 115 MB, YARA Forge core 8 MB, Hashlookup 1 GB). With the full ClamAV databases, clamd uses about 1 GB of memory on the kiosk (measured in the test virtual machine). Signing uses openssl, so that the private key can stay in a hardware token (OpenSSL provider). The release key of the project and its storage are not defined yet.

The command also works on sets built by other means:

pandora-box-signatures build FOLDER --key update.key   # manifest.json + signature
pandora-box-signatures verify FOLDER --keys KEYS_FOLDER
pandora-box-signatures install FOLDER                   # by hand, on a kiosk

build and publish number the set with its creation date (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) unless --serial is given.

docs.title: Online updates
docs.text:
A kiosk works offline by default. An image built with the profile online (Building the image) updates its signatures itself, from their sources: ClamAV (freshclam), YARA Forge, MalwareBazaar and Hashlookup, the sources of pandora-box-signatures publish. The profile brings DHCP on the wired network (IPv4), DNS (systemd-resolved, without LLMNR or mDNS), NTP (systemd-timesyncd, Time), freshclam, the pandora-box-update timer (every 6 hours, 5 minutes after boot), and a firewall that only lets out the update service (TCP), the log export to a SIEM (SIEM), DHCP, DNS and NTP. Nothing comes in but the answers to these connections. It enables the [updates] section of the configuration with every source:

[updates]
enabled = true
sources = ["clamav", "yara-forge", "malwarebazaar", "hashlookup"]
# Optional: a company mirror in place of a source ("clamav": a freshclam
# private mirror), and a proxy
# mirrors = { hashlookup = "https://mirror.example.org/hashlookup-full.bloom" }
# proxy = "http://proxy.example.org:3128"

The kiosk loads the new set the next time it is idle (between two devices): a scan is never interrupted. It logs signatures_changed and shows New signatures installed. Signature update devices are still accepted (a kiosk cut from the network, or signatures newer than the last download).

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
MalwareBazaar needs an abuse.ch Auth-Key (free account: https://auth.abuse.ch/). It is given at build time in image/credentials.toml (see image/credentials.toml.example; git ignores the file), and the profile installs it on the read-only root filesystem as a systemd credential, /etc/credstore/pandora-box.abusech-auth-key, readable by root only: systemd gives it to the update service alone (ImportCredential=). Without it, MalwareBazaar is not downloaded and its database is kept from the last signature update device.

Warning

An image built with credentials must not be published: anyone with the image or the disk of the kiosk can read them.

docs.title: A published set instead
docs.text:
A kiosk can also download a signed set published by pandora-box-signatures publish on a web server, in place of the sources: url (the folder of the set) instead of sources. It then needs no credential, and only installs a set signed with the update key, newer than the installed one, downloading only the files that changed.

The same service also installs online image updates (updates.image_url, see System updates).

docs.title: The update service
docs.text:
pandora-box-update.service runs in two steps (src/pandora_box/online.py):

  1. as the pandora-box-update user, which the firewall lets out, without privileges and in a systemd sandbox, it downloads the sources (with an HTTP cache, /var/lib/pandora-box-update/staging-sources: an unchanged source is not downloaded again; freshclam downloads the daily differences of ClamAV), checks that the engines load them, and builds a set in /var/lib/pandora-box-update/staging when they changed. The files of the sources it does not download are taken from the installed set;
  2. as root, without network, it signs the staged set with the key of the kiosk and installs it (install --staged): every check of a signature update device applies, the unchanged files are taken from the installed set.

The key of the kiosk is an Ed25519 key generated on the kiosk the first time (/var/lib/pandora-box-signatures/local-key/, the private key readable by root only). The kiosk trusts it besides the keys of its image: it verifies the installed set at each start, whoever signed it.

The downloads are HTTPS (a mirror configured in updates.mirrors may be HTTP); the ClamAV databases carry the signature of Cisco Talos, verified by freshclam. freshclam does not load the new databases to test them (TestDatabases no): clamd already holds them in memory, a kiosk has 2 GB. Redirects are only followed to HTTPS URLs, and the proxy of the environment is ignored: only updates.proxy is used.

docs.title: Signature sets
docs.text:
A signature set is a folder holding the signature files of the engines and a signed list of them (src/pandora_box/sigsets.py):

manifest.json          serial, creation date, and the SHA-256 and size of every file
manifest.json.sig      Ed25519 signature of manifest.json
clamav/main.cvd        ClamAV databases (clamd reads this folder)
clamav/daily.cvd
malwarebazaar/malwarebazaar.sha256.bin
hashlookup/hashlookup-full.bloom
yara/yara-forge/yara-rules-core.yar

The paths are those of the default configuration (/var/lib/pandora-box-signatures/current/...). The manifest.json of a subfolder (written by pandora-box-signatures publish) gives the source, version and date of its files; without it, the date of a file is the creation date of the set, used for the signature freshness warnings.

docs.title: Trust
docs.text:
• The kiosk trusts the Ed25519 public keys (*.pem) of signatures.keys, /usr/share/pandora-box/keys/ in the image: they are part of the root filesystem, protected by dm-verity and Secure Boot. The update key is separate from the image signing key: sets are signed far more often.
  • The signature is verified with openssl, on the exact bytes of the manifest, before anything else of the set is read.
  • A set is only installed when its serial is higher than the installed one: an older set, even validly signed, is refused (no rollback).
  • Every file is copied with its size and SHA-256 checked against the manifest; files not listed are ignored; paths are plain names (no .., no hidden name) and links are never followed.
  • The set is installed next to the current one, then a current link is switched atomically: an interrupted update changes nothing. The previous set is kept.
  • At each start, the kiosk verifies the installed set again (signature, then every file) and refuses engine files that are not part of it (signatures.verify). Without a valid set, it scans nothing: it shows NO VALID SIGNATURES and only accepts a signature update device. A new kiosk therefore starts by asking for one.

ClamAV databases (.cvd) are also signed by Cisco Talos and verified by clamd. clamd reads the clamav folder of the installed set (DatabaseDirectory), and is restarted when it changes.

docs.title: Development keys
docs.text:
image/build.sh generates a development key pair, image/update.key and image/update.pem (ignored by git), when they do not exist: the image trusts update.pem, and the test image installs a set signed with update.key. Never use them for a kiosk.

On a development computer, pandora-box-signatures publish without --key builds an unsigned set and prints the matching configuration, with verify = false in [signatures].

docs.title: System updates
docs.text:
The system of a kiosk is read-only: it is updated as a whole, with a new image, never file by file. The disk has two system slots (A/B): the update is written to the free slot while the kiosk runs, and the previous version stays until the new one has booted successfully. The configuration and the theme are part of the image: changing them is also an update.

The signatures are updated separately, far more often: see Signatures.

docs.title: In short
docs.text:
image/build.sh                    # new version, same keys and profile as the kiosk
image/package-update.sh image/mkosi.output/pandora-box.raw update image/update.key
cp -r update /media/$USER/KEY/pandora-box-image

Insert the key into the kiosk: it installs the update and restarts on the new version.

docs.title: Building an update
docs.text:
Build a new version with the same keys as the installed image (its version is the time of the build: newer than the running one), and with the same profile, then package it:

image/build.sh
image/package-update.sh image/mkosi.output/pandora-box.raw update image/update.key

update/ holds the partitions of slot A of the new image (compressed with xz, the format that systemd-sysupdate of Debian 13 decompresses), named with their UUID, the unified kernel image, and a manifest signed with the update key (the format of the signature sets, content image, serial = version). About 215 MB, of which 40 MB for the kernel image.

Two keys protect the update: the update key decides what is installed, the Secure Boot key decides what can boot (the kernel image is signed and holds the root hash of its slot). An update built with other keys is refused, or does not boot.

docs.title: Installing from a USB key
docs.text:
Copy update/ as pandora-box-image/ at the root of a USB key (vfat, exFAT, NTFS or ext4) and insert it into the kiosk (updates.image_from_devices, on by default).

The kiosk verifies the signature, that the version is newer than the running one and every file, copies them to /var/lib/pandora-box-image, then systemd-sysupdate writes the partitions to the free slot and the kernel image to the ESP with 3 boot tries (pandora-box_2+3-0.efi), and the kiosk restarts. The running version is never overwritten; the device is not scanned.

One key can hold a maintenance request, a signature set and an image update: the kiosk handles them in that order, each verified on its own; the image update comes last as it restarts the kiosk.

docs.title: Online
docs.text: With the profile online (Building the image) and updates.image_url, the URL of a published update/ folder, pandora-box-update.service downloads a newer update as its unprivileged user (every file checked), then installs it as root without network (pandora-box-image install), with the same checks as an update device. The kiosk restarts on the new version when it is idle (between two devices): a scan is never interrupted.

docs.title: If the new version fails
docs.text:
The new version is kept (systemd-bless-boot) once boot-complete.target is reached, which requires the kiosk to be ready (Type=notify). A boot that fails restarts: kernel panic (panic=10), failure in the initrd (its emergency shell restarts, image/mkosi.images/initrd/), or no boot-complete.target in 15 minutes. After 3 failed tries, systemd-boot boots the previous version again; the data (/var: reports, quarantine, logs, signatures) is shared by the versions.

boot-entries.txt and boots.txt of a maintenance device show the installed versions and the boots.

docs.title: What is not updated
docs.text: The ESP is not part of the image updates: systemd-boot, its settings and the Secure Boot keys enrolled in the firmware stay as installed. Changing the Secure Boot key needs a new installation.

docs.title: Testing with QEMU
docs.text: The image is tested in a QEMU/KVM virtual machine, without the reference hardware: UEFI firmware (OVMF) with Secure Boot, an empty USB 3 controller, and USB keys inserted and removed while the kiosk runs, which triggers the same udev events as a real device. QEMU runs in the build container: only Docker is needed, and /dev/kvm for speed.

docs.title: In short
docs.text:
image/build-test.sh   # the test image and three image updates
image/vm.sh test      # automated test, about 7 minutes with KVM
image/vm.sh run       # interactive machine, kiosk screen on VNC localhost:0

Note

Hostile samples should only ever be copied into key images, never onto the development desktop.

docs.title: Test profile
docs.text:
--profile test builds pandora-box-test.raw, for the virtual machine tests only, never for a kiosk. It includes the profile online, and adds:

  • a test-only signature set, generated from image/vm/corpus.py, signed with the development update key and installed (serial 1): a ClamAV database that detects the EICAR test file, a MalwareBazaar database, a Hashlookup filter and a YARA rule, each detecting one file of the test key;
  • the matching configuration, with every engine enabled, and online updates from http://10.0.2.2:8080/ (the build container, seen from the QEMU user network);
  • a root shell without password on the virtio console (hvc0), and kernel messages on the serial port;
  • kiosk-screen, which prints the texts of the kiosk screen in that shell (the graphical interface logs them, display_screen events at the DEBUG level);
  • a USBGuard rule for the touch tablet of the virtual machine (QEMU usb-tablet, /etc/usbguard/rules.d/50-vm-test.conf): the test confirms a cleaning with a touch. The keyboard of the virtual machines is not a USB device.

image/build-test.sh builds the test image (version 1) and three signed image updates to newer versions (image/mkosi.output/updates/), for the A/B update test.

docs.title: Automated test
docs.text:
image/build-test.sh
image/vm.sh test

The test boots the test image in QEMU (KVM when /dev/kvm is writable, otherwise much slower emulation), with UEFI firmware (OVMF) where the image signing certificate is enrolled (Secure Boot enabled), and an empty USB 3 controller. It plays the whole user workflow, through QMP and the shell on the virtio console:

  1. the kiosk starts with its five engines and the signature set 1, verified, and no systemd unit fails;
  2. the scan workers (one engine each) run in their sandbox (user, capabilities, no_new_privs, seccomp, network namespace, no device or kiosk data in their file system); Secure Boot is enabled, the kernel is locked down and the root filesystem is on dm-verity;
  3. the root filesystem is read-only EROFS, and /var was grown to fill the 8 GB disk of the machine;
  4. an emulated USB key (a vfat disk image holding the corpus) is inserted, which triggers the same udev events as a real device;
  5. each file gets the expected verdict from the expected engine;
  6. the cleaning is confirmed with a touch on the kiosk screen; the infected files are quarantined (checked against their SHA-256) and removed from the key, which is ejected;
  7. the key is removed: only the clean files are left on it;
  8. the cleaned key is inserted again and reported clean;
  9. keys of the other filesystems go through the same scan and cleaning, then are reported clean: exfat, NTFS, ext4 (its files private to their owner, as on the key of a Linux user) and a key with an MBR partition table and a vfat partition; a key on EROFS (a filesystem the kernel mounts, but not allowed) and an ext4 key whose group descriptors are overwritten are refused; a vfat key with a cut cluster chain is mounted, but the file cannot be read: the key is reported not verified (image/vm/keys.py; exfat and NTFS have no tool writing files without mounting them: they are formatted in the container, then filled by the kernel of the machine, the kiosk stopped);
  10. a signature update key with a newer set (serial 2) is installed, the engines are reloaded and the new sample it detects is found; a modified set, a set signed with another key and an older set are refused; a newer set published on an HTTP server by the test is downloaded by the update service (only its changed file), installed and loaded by the idle kiosk, and only the update service user can open a network connection (systemd-timesyncd alone sends NTP requests); the log entries of the kiosk are sent to a syslog receiver of the test ([siem]), by the SIEM export user, who cannot read the reports; an emulated USB keyboard and network adapter are blocked by USBGuard (no input device, no network interface) and the excluded drivers are not in the image; the kernel settings, the firewall and the service sandboxes are in place;
  11. after a reboot, the scan reports are still there, the root filesystem is unchanged and the signature set 5 is verified at start; a key pressed while the firmware and the boot loader start does not open the boot loader menu;
  12. an image update key to version 2 is inserted: the kiosk installs it in the free slot and restarts, version 2 boots from slot B and is kept (its UKI loses its boot counter), with the same data; version 3, published on an HTTP server by the test, is downloaded and installed by the update service, then the idle kiosk restarts on it and it is kept; finally a version 4 whose root filesystem is modified is installed from a key: it fails 3 boots (dm-verity, the initrd restarts) and systemd-boot goes back to version 3.

Two more machines boot the same image:

  • with a block of the root filesystem modified on the disk (a canary file of the test image): it cannot be read and the kernel reports the corruption;
  • with firmware trusting another key: the firmware refuses systemd-boot ("Access Denied") and nothing starts.

The test also runs lynis (hardening index 73, no warnings) and prints the exposure of the services measured by systemd-analyze security.

The built image is never modified: the machine writes to a new disk overlay (system.qcow2) at every start. It takes about 7 minutes with KVM. image/vm.sh test --workdir DIR keeps the serial console logs, the QEMU logs and the key images in DIR, and the kiosk log (kiosk.log) when the test fails.

docs.title: Interactive machine
docs.text:
image/vm.sh run                                      # test image
image/vm.sh run image/mkosi.output/pandora-box.raw   # production image

The kiosk screen is shown over VNC, display :0 (port 5900), for example with gvncviewer localhost:0 (most viewers read host:N as a display number, port 5900 + N); kiosk-screen also prints it in the shell of the test image. The terminal shows this shell (virtio console), not the kiosk, and, after Ctrl-A C, the QEMU monitor; Ctrl-A X stops the machine.

A production image has no signature set: it shows NO VALID SIGNATURES until a signature update device is inserted, as a new kiosk (Initial installation).

docs.title: Test keys
docs.text:
A test key is created in image/vm/work/usbkey.img; insert and remove it from the QEMU monitor:

(qemu) drive_add 0 if=none,id=key,format=raw,file=/src/image/vm/work/usbkey.img
(qemu) device_add usb-storage,bus=xhci.0,drive=key,id=usbkey,removable=on
(qemu) device_del usbkey

Paths are seen from the container, where the repository is mounted on /src. Any disk image can be used as a key.

docs.title: Real USB keys
docs.text:
A USB key plugged into this computer can be passed through to the machine. List the USB storage devices of this computer, with their port (BUS-PORT) and identifier (VENDOR:PRODUCT):

image/vm.sh usb

1-4  abcd:1234  General UDisk
    sda     3,8G
    └─sda1  3,7G vfat   /media/didier/6B20-F9DE

Then start the machine with --usb, followed by a port, which passes through any key plugged into that port, like the USB port of a kiosk, or by an identifier, which passes through that model of key on any port:

image/vm.sh run --usb 1-4

QEMU attaches the key to the machine as soon as it is plugged in (or at once if it is already there) and takes it from this computer: its kernel driver is detached. Before starting the machine, unmount the key (udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sda1) and disable the automatic mounting of USB devices of the desktop, so that this computer never mounts a key meant for the kiosk. --usb can be given several times. On GNOME:

gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.media-handling automount false
gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.media-handling automount-open false
# after the tests: the same commands with "true"

QEMU then runs as root in the container, with access to the USB devices of this computer and its network (to receive the udev events of the keys plugged in later); the kiosk screen is on localhost:5900 as before.
